title: Config version store: DB schema + migrations + v0 backfill
creator: Michael Nguyen
content:
## Context
We need an immutable version history for Optimize optimization configuration changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing knobs) with safe apply + one-click rollback. This ticket is the foundational storage layer: schema + migrations + retention plumbing + backfill current live configs as version `v0`.

This work unblocks:
- ENG-4822 (list/get/compare versions API)
- ENG-4823 (rollback endpoint)
- Console history + rollback UI (ENG-4825/4826)

References:
- Confluence tech design: `optimize-config-versioning-architecture`
- ADR: `adr-017-config-versioning-storage-and-rollback-semantics`

## Goals
1) Create a durable, query-friendly version store keyed by scope (customer/deployment/region/cluster/route/model).
2) Enforce immutability: versions are append-only; updates only allowed to non-semantic metadata fields (e.g., add link) if ADR permits, otherwise append a new version.
3) Support retention policies (enterprise expectations) without compromising auditability.
4) Backfill: snapshot current live config per scope into version store as `v0` so rollback has a known baseline.

## Non-goals (this ticket)
- Diff generation, apply workflow, validator rules, canary gates (handled in ENG-4822/4824/4827/10511).
- Audit event emission (handled in audit logging workstream, but we must store correlation IDs/refs for joins).

## Proposed storage (per ADR-017)
Postgres (control plane primary). Rationale:
- Strong consistency + transactional semantics for version append + apply pointer updates.
- Operational simplicity (already operated for control plane).
- Works well with pagination/filtering requirements from Console.

## Schema proposal (tables)
### 1) `optimize_config_version`
Append-only rows.

Columns:
- `id` (UUID, PK)
- `scope_hash` (TEXT, NOT NULL) — stable hash of canonical scope fields for efficient lookups
- Scope fields (all TEXT unless noted):
  - `customer_id` (nullable for global/default)
  - `deployment_mode` (ENUM-ish TEXT: hosted|dedicated|private)
  - `environment` (TEXT: prod|staging|dev; required)
  - `region` (nullable)
  - `cluster` (nullable)
  - `route_id` (nullable)
  - `model_id` (nullable)
- `version` (BIGINT, NOT NULL) — monotonically increasing per `scope_hash`
- `config_json` (JSONB, NOT NULL) — full config blob (whole-config rollback)
- `config_sha256` (TEXT, NOT NULL) — hash of canonicalized config_json for idempotency/debug
- `created_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ, NOT NULL, default now())
- `created_by` (TEXT, NOT NULL) — actor identifier (email/service); aligns with authN
- `created_via` (TEXT, NOT NULL) — console|api|automation|migration
- `reason` (TEXT, NULL) — free text justification
- `linked_ticket` (TEXT, NULL) — e.g., LINEAR-123 / JIRA / internal change request
- `request_id` (TEXT, NULL) — for tracing/idempotency (pairs with audit events)

Constraints/Indexes:
- Unique: (`scope_hash`, `version`)
- Indexes:
  - (`scope_hash`, `version` DESC) for latest + pagination
  - (`customer_id`, `created_at` DESC) for per-tenant audit browsing
  - GIN index on `config_json` is *not* planned initially (avoid bloat); revisit if we need server-side filtering on nested fields

### 2) `optimize_config_current`
Single-row pointer per scope to the currently applied version. This avoids scanning `optimize_config_version` for the active record and keeps apply/rollback atomic.

Columns:
- `scope_hash` (TEXT, PK)
- Same scope fields as above (duplicated for filtering + integrity)
- `current_version_id` (UUID, NOT NULL, FK -> optimize_config_version.id)
- `current_version` (BIGINT, NOT NULL) — redundant for convenience
- `updated_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ, NOT NULL)
- `updated_by` (TEXT, NOT NULL)
- `last_apply_request_id` (TEXT, NULL)

Constraints:
- FK ensures pointer references an existing immutable version.

### 3) `optimize_config_retention_policy` (optional for v1; include if easy)
If we need per-tenant overrides.

Columns:
- `customer_id` (TEXT, PK)
- `retention_days` (INT, NOT NULL)
- `min_versions_to_keep` (INT, NOT NULL)
- `created_at`, `updated_at`

Note: Actual deletion is handled by a background job; must be careful not to delete versions referenced by `optimize_config_current` or versions that are within compliance hold.

## Retention semantics
Enterprise expectation is “immutable history” + configurable retention. For initial cut:
- Default: keep 365 days OR last 200 versions per scope (whichever is larger).
- Never delete:
  - the current version
  - the baseline `v0` (backfill snapshot)
- For Private deployments: retention may be customer-controlled; but this ticket is for control-plane Postgres (Hosted/Dedicated). Private is documented separately.

Open question (flagged for Fiona/Marchus in security review): whether we should support legal hold and export requirements now vs later. If later, retention job must be written to be easily extended.

## Migration plan
We will land migrations behind a feature flag `optimize_config_history_enabled`.

Steps:
1) Add tables + constraints.
2) Deploy code that writes `v0` for each existing scope and populates `optimize_config_current` pointers.
3) Verify counts and sampling (see verification plan).
4) Enable flag for internal tenants first; then staged rollout to Hosted prod.

Rollback plan (of this change):
- If migrations cause issues, we can disable the flag. Tables remain but are unused.
- No destructive migration in this phase.

## Backfill plan (v0)
Objective: ensure every scope that currently has a live Optimize config has a baseline version row.

Backfill behavior:
- For each distinct scope in the existing live config store:
  - Create `optimize_config_version` with `version = 0`, `created_via = migration`, `reason = 'baseline import (pre-versioning)'`.
  - Insert/update `optimize_config_current` to point to that version.
- Idempotency:
  - Backfill uses deterministic `scope_hash` + checks for existing (`scope_hash`, `version=0`) before insert.
  - In case of race with new versioning writes (during staged rollout), enforce transactional ordering: pointer update should reference the highest version.

How to compute `scope_hash`:
- Canonical JSON of scope fields (sorted keys, nulls normalized) -> sha256 hex. Must be implemented in a shared library so API + backfill agree.

## Verification
- After backfill, verify:
  - For all scopes S in live config store: exists `optimize_config_current` row and `v0` version row.
  - `optimize_config_current.current_version_id` points to a version with matching scope fields.
  - Sample 100 scopes: `config_sha256` matches recomputed canonicalization.
- Performance:
  - Listing versions for a busy tenant should be <200ms P95 at 50k rows.

## Security/Compliance notes
- `config_json` may contain operational knobs but should not contain secrets. We should still treat it as sensitive operational data.
- Ensure we do not store API keys/tokens in `reason` or other free text fields.
- `created_by` should store stable principal identifier; avoid full JWT payloads.

## Acceptance criteria
- Migrations added with clear forward-only plan; no downtime required.
- Backfill job runnable in staging + prod, idempotent, and produces a `v0` per existing scope.
- `optimize_config_current` pointer exists per scope and references a valid immutable version.
- Retention policy documented; guardrails ensure we never delete current or v0 versions.
- Reviewed by SRE (Sean/Neha) for operational risk and by Security Ops (Fiona) for audit/compliance expectations.

## Implementation notes / tasks
- [x] Draft schema + constraints
- [x] Add `scope_hash` canonicalization helper + tests
- [x] Write migrations
- [ ] Implement backfill worker + metrics (rows_processed, rows_failed, duration)
- [ ] Add admin-only dry-run mode for backfill (count-only)
- [ ] Write verification SQL snippets and attach to runbook

comments: 2025-01-10 — Benji Okafor: Put up an initial schema draft in PR-10432. Still debating whether `optimize_config_current` should live in same DB vs config service. Leaning same DB for atomicity (apply pointer update + insert version in one txn).

2025-01-13 — Chloe Martin: +1 on `optimize_config_current`. Console needs a cheap way to show “current version” without scanning. Also helps avoid weirdness when two versions share same created_at ordering.

2025-01-15 — Sean Gallagher: Please add explicit rollback plan for the migration itself (what happens if backfill partially succeeds). We need a deterministic retry story and a way to validate completeness before enabling UI.

2025-01-17 — Michael Nguyen: Added idempotency notes: ensure unique constraint on (scope_hash, version) and backfill checks for v0. Will also add a metric + dashboard panel for percent of scopes with v0 created.

2025-01-22 — Fiona McCarthy: Retention language needs to be precise: ‘immutable’ means operators can’t edit history, but retention still allows deletion under policy. Ensure we never delete versions referenced by current pointer; also document redaction expectations for free-text fields (reason/ticket links).

2025-01-29 — Benji Okafor: Implemented canonicalization + scope_hash helper with unit tests. Next step: backfill worker (batching by customer_id to avoid long transactions). Planning to emit request_id = backfill-run-<timestamp> to join with audit events later.

2025-02-03 — Neha Kapoor: Before we go past staging, I want a one-pager of verification queries + expected row counts for Hosted prod. Also ensure the backfill worker has a max-QPS / sleep knob so we don’t saturate primary.
